name: Security Analysis Benchmark Lite v1
description: Fast eight-case subset covering SQL injection and OS command injection across all four analysis axes.
system_prompt: You are evaluating application security code. Follow the requested response format exactly and return only the requested verdict or option token. Analyze actual attacker-controlled data flow, security boundaries, dangerous sinks, and whether the proposed defense preserves functionality. Do not add explanations.

tests.rationale: The request-controlled email value is concatenated into SQL text before the database executes it.

provenance.basis: CWE-89 true-positive source-to-SQL-sink pattern with direct string construction.

tests.rationale: The SQL statement remains constant and the attacker-controlled email is passed only as a bound parameter.

provenance.basis: CWE-89 false-positive control using a prepared statement and bound request data.

tests.rationale: Only option B follows the attacker-controlled query parameter through SQL string construction into the database execution sink.

provenance.basis: CWE-89 source-to-sink trace derived from executable SQL injection test patterns.

tests.rationale: Option A removes SQL syntax control by keeping query text constant and binding the email value separately.

provenance.basis: CWE-89 remediation using parameterized SQL while preserving lookup behavior.

tests.rationale: The request-controlled archive name is inserted into a shell command interpreted by exec.

provenance.basis: CWE-78 true-positive request-source to shell-command sink pattern.

tests.rationale: The archive name is allowlisted and passed as a distinct argument to tar without shell interpretation.

provenance.basis: CWE-78 false-positive control using non-shell execution and finite-domain validation.

tests.rationale: Only option C traces the request body through command-string concatenation into a shell-interpreted exec call.

provenance.basis: CWE-78 source-to-sink trace derived from executable command injection patterns.

tests.rationale: Option A validates the finite archive-name domain and removes shell parsing by separating executable arguments.

provenance.basis: CWE-78 remediation using allowlist validation and direct process execution.
